29.88051,-97.95226: Kone-Yarbrough House. This Victorian residence with its unusual central chimney was erected in 1886 for the growing family of Sam R. 29.88175,-97.94931: George Thomas McGehee House. 29.88185,-97.95058: George Henry Talmadge Home. A farmer from Illinois, George H. Talmadge (1840-1911) served in the Union Army during the Civil War. 29.88187,-97.94263: The Calaboose. Constructed as the first Hays County Jail in 1873, this small brick structure was later an annex for black prisoners. 29.88211,-97.95037: Eliza Pitts Malone. In 1842, Eliza Pitts (1832-1923) and her parents came to Texas from Georgia. 29.88217,-97.94291: First Christian Church of San Marcos. Formed by the Rev. Henry Thomas in 1853 with only two members, the congregation had grown to fifty members by 1856. 29.88255,-97.67215: Cardwell Home. John Madison Cardwell (1838-1917) moved to Caldwell county at the age of eighteen. 29.88261,-97.95023: O. T. Brown Home. Built in 1878, this residence was purchased in 1882 by Georgia native O. T. 29.883,-97.95045: Kone-Cliett House. 29.8831,-97.94874: Caldwell-Kone-Hyatt House. Robert M. Caldwell (1836-84), son of pioneer Texas colonists, built this house in 1869. His wife, Mary, was a sister of Col. E. M. 29.88578,-97.93859: William W. Moon. (March 25, 1814 - Jan. 7, 1897) Orphaned two days after his birth, William W. Moon grew up with two uncles in his native Alabama. 29.88591,-97.95004: Robert Early McKie House. This house was built by local contractor H. C.
